overview: Wladyslaw II Jagiello was grand duke of Lithuania and king of Poland, founder of the Jagiellonian dynasty’s power, and victor at Grunwald.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Wladyslaw II Jagiello was grand duke of Lithuania and king of Poland, founder of the Jagiellonian dynasty’s power, and victor at Grunwald.

contentSections.title: Birth and early life
paragraphs: Wladyslaw II Jagiello was born c. 1352, associated with Lithuania. The early evidence is uneven, so precise details should be treated carefully.
His background belonged to the world of Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania, where dynastic claims, military service, and aristocratic alliances shaped political careers.

contentSections.title: Character and Personality
paragraphs: Władysław II Jagiełło is remembered as the Lithuanian grand duke who became a Polish king and a Christian convert, and the sources — Polish, and notably the chronicler Jan Długosz — present a complex figure not always to their taste. He came to the Polish throne through marriage and through his acceptance of Christianity, uniting Poland and Lithuania, and Długosz, while acknowledging his achievements, often portrayed him as cautious, reserved, and shaped by his pagan Lithuanian origins.

His most celebrated moment was the great victory over the Teutonic Order at the Battle of Grunwald in 1410, where the sources credit him with patient generalship — notably his deliberate, prayerful slowness in committing to battle, which his critics read as hesitation and his admirers as prudence. That ambiguity runs through his portrayal: a careful, devout, and politically shrewd ruler whose restraint could look like either wisdom or timidity.

Because the main source viewed him through a Polish and clerical lens not wholly sympathetic to his Lithuanian background, the portrait carries a faint condescension that modern historians discount. What emerges is a long-reigning, patient, and consequential ruler — founder of a dynasty and of the Polish-Lithuanian union — remembered for the deliberate, unflashy statecraft that won Grunwald and bound two realms together.

contentSections.title: As king of Poland and grand duke of Lithuania
paragraphs: Jogaila’s conversion and marriage to Jadwiga joined Polish and Lithuanian politics. At Grunwald, his coalition defeated the Teutonic Order in one of medieval Europe’s largest battles.
Battle of Grunwald gives Wladyslaw II Jagiello's career a specific military and political setting: his choices, command, defeat, or death affected the outcome remembered in that article.

contentSections.title: Death
paragraphs: Died at Horodok in 1434 after a reign that joined Polish kingship with Lithuanian dynastic power.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: He is remembered as a dynastic founder and as one of the rulers who broke Teutonic military dominance in the Baltic region.

keyAchievements.title: United Polish and Lithuanian politics
keyAchievements.description: Jogaila’s conversion and marriage to Jadwiga joined Lithuanian and Polish politics in a durable dynastic union.

keyAchievements.title: Founded Jagiellonian royal power
keyAchievements.description: His reign established the Jagiellonian dynasty as a major force in central and eastern Europe.

keyAchievements.title: Won the Battle of Grunwald
keyAchievements.description: Grunwald checked Teutonic Order power and became a defining victory for the Polish-Lithuanian alliance.
